info.title: MoneyMoney API
info.description: Personal finance assistant: chat, transactions, and summaries.

get.description: The caller's signed-in sessions, this one first.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api V1 Auth Sessions Get

delete.description: Sign out one of the caller's devices. Another user's session id is a 404.

post.description: Sign out every device except the one making this request.

Change the caller's password; every other device is signed out, this one stays in.

It checks the current password, so it is rate-limited like login: a stolen session must
not become a way to guess the password.

schema.title: Response List Categories Api V1 Categories Get
Response List Accounts Api V1 Accounts Get

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Client-generated key; repeating it returns the original transaction.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: Client-generated key; repeating it returns the original transaction.

get.description: Totals for a period in the user's own calendar, grouped by currency.
Transcript plus any question the assistant is still waiting on (resume after refresh).

post.description: Non-streaming variant for server-to-server callers (MCP tools, integrations).

200.description: Server-sent events. Each event's `data` is a JSON `TurnEvent`; the stream ends after `turn.completed` or `error`.

AccountCreate.title: AccountCreate
AccountCreate.description: A new account. Without a currency it takes the user's base currency.

AccountRef.title: AccountRef
AccountRef.description: A compact reference to an account, as transactions show it.

AccountUpdate.title: AccountUpdate
AccountUpdate.description:
Partial update: a field left out (or null) stays as it is.

There is no `currency`: an account's currency is fixed when it is created, so sending
one is rejected like any other unknown field.

AccountView.title: AccountView
AccountView.description: An account as clients see it. An archived account stays on past transactions.

CategoryRef.title: CategoryRef
CategoryRef.description: A compact reference to a category, as transactions and merchant rules show it.

DraftPreview.title: DraftPreview
DraftPreview.description: What the assistant has understood so far, shown next to a question.

InteractionResponse.title: InteractionResponse
InteractionResponse.description: The user's answer to a pending clarification or confirmation.

MerchantRuleUpdate.title: MerchantRuleUpdate
MerchantRuleUpdate.description: A change to a rule: the category its merchant is filed under from now on.

MerchantRuleView.title: MerchantRuleView
MerchantRuleView.description: One learned rule: the merchant, the category it files them under, and how often.

MoneyAmount.title: MoneyAmount
MoneyAmount.description: An exact amount. `amount` is a decimal string; never parse it as a float.

PasswordChange.title: PasswordChange
PasswordChange.description: A signed-in user replacing their password; the current one proves it is them.

RevokedSessionsView.title: RevokedSessionsView
RevokedSessionsView.description: How many sessions a "sign out all other devices" request signed out.

device.title: Device
device.description: Best guess from the User-Agent, e.g. "Chrome on Windows".

lastSeenAt.title: Lastseenat
lastSeenAt.description: Refreshed at most once an hour.

isCurrent.title: Iscurrent
isCurrent.description: True for the session making this request.

SessionView.title: SessionView
SessionView.description: One signed-in browser or device, as the user sees it in Settings → Security.

SpendingSummary.title: SpendingSummary
SpendingSummary.description:
Totals for one period, computed in SQL from the ledger (never by the model).

Amounts are grouped per currency: values in different currencies are never summed.

TransactionUpdate.title: TransactionUpdate
TransactionUpdate.description:
Partial update. Only fields present in the request change; `null` clears a field.

`version` must match the stored version (optimistic concurrency): a stale edit from
another tab gets a 409 instead of silently overwriting newer data.
